newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Most Palestinians back peace moves with Israel.
newsitem.headline: Most Palestinians back peace moves with Israel.

text.p: A Palestinian opinion poll published on Wednesday showed there was still overwhelming support in the West Bank and Gaza Strip for Israel-PLO peace moves.
According to the study, conducted by the Jerusalem Media and Communciation Centre (JMCC), 78.1 percent of Palestinians polled said they still support the peace process launched in 1991.
In response to another question, 74.9 percent said they strongly or cautiously support Israel-PLO peace deals signed since 1993 giving Palestinians self-rule in much of the West Bank and Gaza.
Israel-PLO peace moves were set back by the election last May of hardline Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu who opposed the agreements reached under the previous left-leaning government.

But officials on both sides said on Wednesday they were close to reaching a deal on a long overdue Israeli redeployment from Hebron, the last Palestinian West Bank town due for self-rule under a peace agreement signed more than a year ago.
The JMCC said it questioned 1,152 in person in the West Bank and Gaza Strip on December 13 and 14. The poll's margin of error was three percent.
A survey published by the Nablus-based Centre of Palestine Research and Studies in October after a wave of clashes in the West Bank and Gaza Strip put support for the peace process at 69.8 percent.
Sixty Palestinians and 15 Israelis were killed in the September clashes, which erupted after Israel opened a second entrance to an archaeological tunnel near a Moslem shrine in Jerusalem.
